stem:
What part of speech is the word "friendly" in this sentence?

The friendly clerk helped us.
hints: Do not decide by the ending alone. Look at which word "friendly" describes.
Ask: friendly describes what? Then ask whether that word is a noun or a verb.
A word that describes a noun is an adjective. A word that describes a verb is an adverb. Find what "friendly" describes, then decide.

steps.action: Find the word that "friendly" describes: the friendly clerk.
steps.why: It comes right before "clerk" and tells what kind of clerk.

steps.action: "clerk" names a person, so it is a noun.
A word that describes a noun is an adjective.
steps.why: Many adverbs end in -ly, like softly and quickly. But not every -ly word is an adverb. Friendly, lovely and costly describe nouns.

trapNotes.Adverb: Many adverbs end in -ly, so this is the easy trap. But adverbs describe verbs. Friendly describes the clerk, which is a noun.
trapNotes.Noun: Friendly does not name a person or thing. It tells what kind of clerk.
trapNotes.Verb: The action here is "helped". Friendly is not something the clerk did; it describes the clerk.
